symptom: In the Terrain map view, Google's own black country-border line visibly drifts away from our green SVG-drawn Romania border, worst near the edges of the viewport (e.g. the Moldova/Ukraine border, the Black Sea coast) and least near the center of the current view.
rootcause: Two different, fundamentally incompatible projections are stacked on top of each other. Google Maps always renders its base layer (including the administrative-border line) in Web Mercator, where north-south (latitude) scale increases with distance from the equator (a sec(lat) factor). Our SVG overlay -- countyOutlines.ts, romaniaGraph.ts city positions -- is deliberately drawn with a plain linear equirectangular projection ('no distortion, bounding-box fit', per lib/countyOutlines.ts's own header comment), so the schematic diagram stays clean and undistorted. The two projections agree exactly on longitude (both scale it linearly), but diverge on latitude, and the divergence grows with |lat - reference_lat|, i.e. with distance from the view's center -- exactly the observed pattern. This was verified NOT to be the smaller, separate issue of an imperfect city-position projection fit: refitting components/search/SearchMap.tsx's PROJECTION constants via least squares against all 20 known city lon/lat control points reproduced the exact same constants already in scripts/lib/project.mjs (to 6 decimal places) -- i.e. that transform is already the global optimum for the committed SVG city positions, and the residual (largest ~6px, at Neamt/Oradea) is unrelated hand-layout noise in the original diagram, not a fixable calibration bug. A second check confirmed the city positions fit a linear latitude model better than a Mercator-transformed one (RMSE 1.6 vs 1.8), i.e. the SVG diagram truly is linear/equirectangular by construction, not an approximation of Mercator. So the border mismatch is structural: a real Mercator-projected border line will never coincide with a linear-equirectangular one except at one calibration latitude.
fix:
Rather than chase pixel alignment (impossible without either re-projecting every piece of committed SVG geometry to Web Mercator, or moving the whole background to a projection-controllable renderer like MapLibre -- both large, out-of-scope changes), Google's own country-boundary stroke was turned off on the Terrain layer via the map style array (components/search/SearchMap.tsx, TERRAIN_MAP_STYLES: added `{ featureType: 'administrative.country', elementType: 'geometry.stroke', stylers: [{ visibility: 'off' }] }`), so only our own single, deliberately-schematic green border is shown. Same reasoning already applied earlier in the same style array to hide Google's own place-name labels in favor of our own SVG labels.

Update (2026-09-16, same day): the identical root cause also showed up for roads -- a thin sliver of Google's own real road visibly peeking out from under our thicker route line at curves (e.g. the Mehadia-Lugoj mountain pass), worst on roads spanning more latitude. Unlike the border, this WAS fixed by re-projecting, not hiding, because (unlike countyOutlines.ts) every road/city coordinate is a known invertible equirectangular transform with no external GIS data needed: new lib/mercatorProjection.ts unprojects each committed [x,y] back to lon/lat via the existing PROJECTION/unprojectToLatLng (moved there from SearchMap.tsx), then reprojects latitude only (longitude is identical in both projections) through a Web Mercator formula, least-squares-fit to the same 20 city control points (MERCATOR_LAT_SCALE/MERCATOR_LAT_OFFSET). This produces mercatorCityPositions and mercatorRoadGeometry, parallel precomputed tables alongside the existing equirectangular ones. lib/roadPath.ts's getRoadPoints/getRoadPathD gained an optional `variant: "default" | "mercator"` parameter (cache key updated to include it) so the existing pure drawing helpers stay coordinate-system-agnostic -- SearchMap.tsx just picks which table to read from via `roadVariant = displayMode === "default" ? "default" : "mercator"`, applied to the road base layer, road labels, city nodes, and all four trace-line families (SearchTreeLines/ExpandedTreeLines/PathLines/GraphLine, which already funneled through one shared getRoadPathD call). The Default view is completely unaffected -- it never reads the mercator tables. PathDots (the county-clipped route-progress dot texture) was deliberately left on the default/equirectangular variant always: it's a decorative density texture clipped by county polygons (which stay equirectangular, per the border fix above), not a marker that needs to ride exactly on the drawn line, so re-projecting only its road-distance calculation would have desynced it from the (unmoved) county clip regions for no benefit.
automation_gap: Visual/pixel alignment between the Google tile background and the SVG overlay cannot be asserted by any existing gate (all are JSON/unit-test based, nothing renders or screenshots the composited map). For the border, the prevention is architectural, not testable: don't rely on Google's (or any Mercator-based) own border/label rendering to visually agree with our schematic SVG layer -- always suppress the competing feature via TERRAIN_MAP_STYLES rather than trying to align it. For roads/cities, the prevention is the opposite direction -- reproject our own geometry to Mercator via lib/mercatorProjection.ts rather than hide Google's road layer (which would also erase real-world context outside our 23 edges) -- also left as a documented convention, verified only by manual zoomed-in comparison against the live Google layer, not a script check.
notes:
Precedent: scripts/fetch_neighboring_context.mjs already documents the identical category of bug for a different pairing -- our county outlines vs. Natural Earth's neighboring-country borders not landing on identical pixels -- and solves it by inflating neighbor shapes outward so the seam is hidden underneath Romania's opaque layer. This is the same root problem (two different real-world border datasets/projections never coincide exactly) showing up a second time, now against Google's live basemap tiles.

Reconciled (2026-09-16): this note previously said any future MapLibre work should move Google toward equirectangular rather than move our SVG toward Mercator. Roads went the opposite direction here (our SVG toward Mercator) for a good, narrow reason -- MapLibre isn't built, and unlike the border, roads/cities have committed, invertible source coordinates that make a faithful Mercator reprojection possible with zero new external data or network calls. The border stays hidden-not-reprojected because lib/countyOutlines.ts has no committed source lon/lat or generator script (single commit, no companion script, confirmed via `git log --follow`) to reproject from reliably. If MapLibre is ever built, prefer letting it render in plain equirectangular so nothing needs reprojecting or hiding at all -- but until then, this repo now has two data-driven building blocks worth knowing about: TERRAIN_MAP_STYLES (suppress Google's competing feature) and lib/mercatorProjection.ts (reproject our own geometry to match Google) -- pick whichever applies to whatever's mismatched, roughly per the same rule used above.
